physics_scope: Opt-in conservative positive continuous emitted-intensity/LD moments on original curvature fields. Source thermal, reflection, passband and table evaluations retain prior equations. Existing API uses constant cells. Circular detached supported scope and full CPU routing remain explicit.
provenance: The final per-instance non-reentrancy guard rejects overlapping calls before active field arrays can be cleared. Two CPU and two hardware controls on the published source include rejection during actual flux integration and a changed-candidate batch. The timed science kernels are unchanged.
CPU reference uses independent original trigonometric roots, NumPy solves, curved area integration and original ELISa LD/flux/mapping/density routines on this finite model.

First timings (173–183) use a repeated per-node parent condition SVD on reference CPU. Final source reuses the identical precomputed per-face condition while preserving the independent solve. 185/187/190/192/194 use that optimized reference. GPU and JAX CPU geometry and kernels are identical across the optimization. Full B1/B4 original/optimized CPU outputs verified bitwise.

Physical constants and asset digest are recorded per profile. A CPU-forced standalone original CLI matches the m020 published two-sample reference bitwise. pytest selects historical Astropy constants and equivalent comparisons must use matching runtime conventions.

Earlier CPU fixture setup and golden-test failures are retained privately. Corrected fixture LD law, slice-order and process conventions. Accepted CPU controls are the union of passing case identities.

CPU-only fine checks use cores16–19 nice19 and serve as accuracy controls. They overlapped part of the initial bounded series. Matched costs use timed processes on cores0–15 nice10 and the recorded single-thread BLAS/OMP environment. Independent B1 repeat and timing distributions included; B4/B8 have one changed warm measurement each.

Enclosing timers include construction, transfers, host outputs, prior, original observation mapping, density and accuracy checks on two finite curves. The GPU controller visits individual candidates/phases. Programs may compile new shapes even on changed warm calls. Profiled times and occupancy samples are separate from unprofiled throughput.

Each finite profile includes complete component/raw/normalized curves. Other profiles retain per-proposal curve/trace hashes, predictions, field conservation diagnostics, densities and timed samples. Times for nested stages overlap and are not additive.
